etymologies.etymologyHTML: From wood +‎ pecker. Compare Middle English wod spek (“woodpecker”), Middle English wodehake (“woodpecker”), Middle English wodewale (“woodpecker”). Displaced speight.

definitions.definition: Any bird of species-rich family Picidae, with a strong pointed beak suitable for pecking holes in wood.

quote.citation: 1886, Peter Christen Asbjørnsen, translated by H.L. Brækstad, Folk and Fairy Tales, page 89:
quote.text: On its summit towered aloft the fir tree which has often been referred to, like a mighty mast, full of woodpeckers' holes.

quote.citation: 1922, E[ric] R[ücker] Eddison, The Worm Ouroboros‎[1], London: Jonathan Cape, page 19:
quote.text: His skin was scarlet like the head of the green woodpecker.

quote.citation: 1928 August, Outram Bangs, James L. Peters, “Birds Collected by Dr. Joseph F. Rock in Western Kansu and Eastern Tibet”, in Bulletin of the Museum of Comparative Zoölogy‎[2], volume LXVIII, number 7, Cambridge, Mass.: Harvard College, →OCLC, page 333:
quote.text: An adult female of this rare woodpecker was taken at 6,000 feet in April 1925 near Chingchuan in the forests of northern Szechuan.

quote.citation: 1984, Virginia Wildlife, volume 45, Virginia Commission of Game and Inland Fisheries:
quote.text: Birdwatchers would enjoy a host of sparrows, a herd of swans, a descent of woodpeckers, a herd of wrens, and mutation of thrushes.

definitions.definition: (military slang) The Type 92 heavy machine gun.
